messages:
Sam (Support): Hi @Marta — Acme just escalated: Dedicated endpoint behind their VPC L7 proxy started returning 403 after they switched to signed cookies. They pasted a curl and some logs. Can you share the curl they used so we can repro?

Marta (Customer Success): ```
curl -v 'https://dedicated.acme.internal/predict' \
  -H 'Cookie: acme_auth=SIGNED(eyJhbGci...)' \
  -H 'X-Request-Id: 8a2f' \
  --data '{"input": "hello"}'
```

Sam (Support): Thanks. FYI our runtime logs show 403 with a missing header error from the dedicated nodes: 

Sam (Support): ```
2026-03-12T14:22:01Z runtime ERROR request_id=8a2f auth=missing_header 403 "missing x-redwood-sub or Authorization"
```

Sam (Support): The expectation is either Authorization: Bearer <token> forwarded or an X-Redwood-Sub header with the decoded subject. If the L7 is relying on signed cookies only, we need the cookie-to-header translation preserved. @Priya any LB changes recently that would affect header preservation? :thinking:

Priya (Eng Platform): Not intentionally. We shipped a response Set-Cookie strip for hosted last week but that shouldn't affect ingress for Dedicated. Our config does have a header-preserve toggle, though — most clusters default to false to avoid leaking internal headers. @Jorge can you check the ext_authz plugin behavior for signed cookies?

Jorge (Eng Infra): Quick grep of the envoy filter: our ext_authz plugin decodes JWTs when present in Authorization or X-Forwarded-User but DOES NOT decode signed cookies. Also, some customer L7 setups terminate TLS and re-issue the cookie, which can cause the proxy chain to rewrite cookies and drop custom headers. If the internal proxy rewrites Cookie then our LB might see a cookie but not the intermediary Authorization header.

Marta (Customer Success): We're seeing intermittent 403s — some requests pass. Example from their packet capture: between acme-internal-l7 -> our LB there's an Authorization header, but when it reaches our dedicated node pool it's missing. So looks like a hop is stripping it.

Sam (Support): Repro from Acme (condensed):
1) Client -> acme-frontend (sets signed cookie)
2) acme-frontend -> internal L7 (cookie preserved)
3) internal L7 -> our LB (they say Authorization header present)
4) our LB -> dedicated nodes (we see no header)

Sam (Support): That points at our LB/Envoy config dropping or normalizing headers when certain cookie patterns exist. Can we try a config toggle to preserve headers and see if that eliminates the 403s?

Priya (Eng Platform): There's a per-cluster flag `preserve_incoming_headers`. Default false. Setting it true will preserve incoming headers and avoid aggressive header sanitization. That seems like a safe mitigation for this customer. Long-term we should add signed-cookie decode into ext_authz.

Jorge (Eng Infra): I'll flip the flag on the staging copy for Acme now. @auth-bot run auth-config-check acme-vpc

auth-bot: auth-config-check: acme-vpc -> ext_authz v1.3 detected, cookie_rewrite=false, preserve_incoming_headers=false

Jorge (Eng Infra): Applying preserve_incoming_headers=true on staging and reloading envoy... reload complete.

Marta (Customer Success): Acme re-ran their smoke tests against staging: 20/20 requests returned 200 OK, no 403 observed. They confirmed Authorization header is present end-to-end now. :tada:

Sam (Support): Nice. Root cause summary for internal notes: our ext_authz lacked signed-cookie decoding and the dedicated LB had header-preserve off. In chains where customer proxies terminate TLS and re-issue cookies, header rewriting removed the Authorization/X-Redwood headers before hitting the runtime, causing auth to fail. Immediate mitigation: enable preserve_incoming_headers for affected clusters. Permanent fix: add signed-cookie JWT decode path in ext_authz and a safe cookie->header rewrite option.

Priya (Eng Platform): I'll open a ticket to make preserve_incoming_headers configurable per cluster (ENGPLAT-2547) and add a rollout plan.

Jorge (Eng Infra): Filed INFRA-4321: Add signed-cookie JWT decode to ext_authz and a non-destructive cookie-to-header rewrite mode. Assigned to infra-auth, ETA ~2w.

Sam (Support): I'll update Acme with the mitigation and ETA for the platform fix. Marta can you handle the customer communication and a short KB with repro and recommended LB config?

Marta (Customer Success): Yep — will publish KB titled "Dedicated endpoints + signed cookies: header preservation and recommended LB settings" and coordinate with account team.

Sam (Support): Thanks everyone, closing this support escalation once KB is published. :thumbsup:
